approaches.make_before_break_note: the TCP baseline does not use link overlap (it does not pre-establish the new connection), so an MBB run would just delay link release
approaches.mechanism: The address change kills the TCP connection. The app detects it (OS notification, or a stall timeout), opens a new connection from the new address and resumes the session with its own sequence numbers (HELLO carries the next needed seq).
approaches.mobility_overhead: none specific to mobility (the peer sees a new address and a new connection)
approaches.name: TCP reconnection baseline
approaches.recovery_point: first new (non-duplicate) data frame delivered to the mobile node on the NEW connection
approaches.scope_limits: Needs an application that implements resume; an unmodified TCP application simply loses its connection.
approaches.standards_status: No mobility protocol. Application-level behaviour over TCP (RFC 9293). In the emulator TCP is the simplified TcpLite model; the same application logic is validated over real kernel TCP on loopback.

approaches.make_before_break_note: basic Mobile IP is break-before-make by definition here; use approach 'mip-mbb' for the overlap variant
approaches.mechanism: Registration with the Home Agent (signed, replay-protected); the Home Agent tunnels (IP-in-IP) packets for the home address to the current care-of address; replies go direct (triangle routing).
approaches.mobility_overhead: 20 bytes of IP-in-IP header per packet on the forward path (via the Home Agent)
approaches.name: Basic Mobile IP
approaches.recovery_point: first accepted registration reply (the Home Agent now tunnels to the new care-of address)
approaches.scope_limits: Break-before-make: the old link disappears with the movement.
approaches.standards_status: Educational Mobile IPv4-style demonstration (Stage 4). NOT RFC 5944 compliant: HMAC-SHA256 instead of keyed-MD5, no Foreign Agent, no ARP, no reverse tunnelling (see docs/MOBILE_IP.md).

approaches.name: Mobile IP with make-before-break handoff
approaches.scope_limits: Requires two simultaneously usable links; benefit depends on the hold time (drain) of the old link.
approaches.standards_status: Basic Mobile IP (above) with an overlap period: the new link is up before the old one is released. approaches.mechanism: Basic Mobile IP registration plus a Return Routability exchange (home + care-of tokens) and an authenticated Binding Update to the correspondent, which then sends directly to the care-of address (IP-in-IP stand-in for the IPv6 routing header).
approaches.mobility_overhead: 20 bytes of IP-in-IP header per packet on the DIRECT path (Mobile IPv6 uses a 24-byte routing header)
approaches.name: Simplified route-optimisation model
approaches.recovery_point: Binding Update accepted by the correspondent (route-optimised path active)
approaches.scope_limits: The correspondent keeps using the old care-of address until the new binding is accepted, so handoff can be slower than via the home agent.
approaches.standards_status: SIMPLIFIED MODEL inspired by Mobile IPv6 route optimisation (RFC 6275). Route optimisation belongs to Mobile IPv6, not Mobile IPv4. This is NOT Mobile IPv6 and NOT a standards implementation (see app/mobileip/ro.py).

approaches.make_before_break_note: this harness does not exploit link overlap (no probing of the new path before the old one is released)
approaches.mechanism: The client app keeps ONE QUIC connection; when its local address changes it sends from the new address with a fresh connection ID; the server validates the new path (PATH_CHALLENGE/RESPONSE) and continues the same streams.
approaches.name: QUIC connection migration
approaches.recovery_point: first new data delivered to the mobile node after the address change (path validation is not exposed by the aioquic API)
approaches.scope_limits: Works only for applications that use QUIC. It does NOT make arbitrary TCP applications mobile.
approaches.standards_status: Real QUIC engine (aioquic) in the emulator (RFC 9000 section 9 connection migration). Requires aioquic.
